checks: A primitive mth root of unity lies in the cyclic norm-one group of order q+1. The standard Hermitian form is nondegenerate.
The shift preserves the orthonormal basis and the clock diagonal has norm-one entries. For odd m both determinants are1, including characteristic2.
XY=zeta^-1 YX, and the commutator scalar has norm one and determinant1, so the projective matrices commute in PSU.
If X^aY^b is scalar, its coordinate-line permutation forces a=0 and its first two diagonal entries force b=0. The projective subgroup is exactly (Z/m)^2.
The set-theoretic section gives c((a,b),(a_prime,b_prime))=zeta^(b*a_prime), with no exponent-carry scalar. Its pointwise mth power is1.

A coboundary on an abelian group with trivial coefficients is symmetric. The alternating ratio on the two coordinate generators is zeta^-1, so any annihilating exponent is divisible by m. The class has exact order m in H2 with coefficients K^times itself.
The field character is trivial, so the full semilinear scalar extension restricts to this exact ordinary extension.
At fixed p=2 use q=2^f,m=q+1 with f>=2. At fixed odd p use even f,q=p^f,m=(q+1)/2; q=1 mod8 makes m odd. Both families are unbounded and can be kept in the known simple ranges m>=5.

No assertion of realization or exact geometric Brauer order on one fixed surface group, and no claim against a hereditary representation bound. This is a failed uniform algebraic period shortcut only.
